reasons: Claimed status is compliant and consistent with the artifacts: the redline is identical to the original paragraph and no comment is raised, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

Section 14.1 meets the fallback on its material terms — a mutual right to assign in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, with consent required for other assignments — and the deterministic check confirms the successor/M&A carve-out for Customer is present.

No walk-away trigger exists: there is no blanket prohibition on Customer assignment (the M&A carve-out is express) and no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on Customer's change of control; the rationale correctly notes §11.2 triggers are limited to uncured material breach and insolvency.

The two shortfalls versus the preferred position (no express affiliate carve-out, consent not qualified as 'not to be unreasonably withheld', no notice mechanic) are correctly recorded in the rationale rather than redlined, per the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements.
The mutual 'direct competitor' consent exception is accurately characterized as symmetrical and not adverse on balance, so it does not convert the clause into a deviation.
